payload.claim: No test ever confirms that `mutate`'s exit actually attempts and completes a restore when the interrupted run's file was otherwise fine — every interrupt scenario here (this one and `test_a_restore_that_cannot_read_the_file_does_not_replace_the_interrupt`) first corrupts or deletes the file, so `KeyboardInterrupt` propagates whether or not `restore_mutant` was ever called. The spy-based `test_an_interrupt_still_propagates_through_the_new_seam` only checks an `entered`/`exited` event list from a hand-written context manager, never `_mutated` itself, so it proves nothing about `saffron/mutation.py`'s real restore path either. Edit `_mutated` (saffron/mutation.py) to `try: yield None\nexcept BaseException:\n    raise` before the restore attempt — skipping `restore_mutant` entirely whenever any exception (including `KeyboardInterrupt`) is propagating through the block — and every test in this suite, including this one, still passes, even though the tree is now left permanently mutated on every interrupted run, which is exactly the class of defect this refactor's docstring says the new seam exists to prevent.
